name: Jev 1.13

pricing_usd_per_mtok.notes: TypeSafe charges input tokens only ($42 per billion); output tokens are reported but free; no cache price, free tier, per-question fee or minimum is published; prepaid credits under the customer agreement

benchmarks.name: JevBench v1.5.6 capability score (1,624 decisions: 904 open, 720 sealed)
benchmarks.setting: jev-1.13.0, hosted API; sub-scores Intelligence 72.0, Calibration 88.0
benchmarks.harness: Benchmark Heaven's own runner (the measurer also sells custom evaluations)

benchmarks.name: TypeSafe workflow evals, overview (agreement with reference labels, percent, mean of four workflows)
benchmarks.setting: Jev in workflow mode; reference labels are the average of GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 at high thinking, so the score is agreement with two LLMs, not accuracy against people
benchmarks.harness: TypeSafe's own workflows, built by its model-capabilities team

benchmarks.name: Entagl authored decision cases (accuracy, percent, 1,357 scored decisions over 283 cases)
benchmarks.setting: jev-1.13.0; hard cases run three times; 13 languages; an unnamed frontier Gemini model at low reasoning effort scored 99.0 on the same cases
benchmarks.harness: Entagl's own cases from its direct-message agent product; no public raw corpus

benchmarks.name: Distil Labs invoice pay-or-hold (accuracy, 100 synthetic invoices)
benchmarks.setting: average of three request formulations (0.77, 0.75, 0.84); one run each; the vendor's own fine-tuned Qwen3.5-4B scored 0.98
benchmarks.harness: Distil Labs' published pipeline; Distil sells fine-tuning, so it competes with Jev

benchmarks.name: Kev project breadth-v1 test, chance-corrected index
benchmarks.setting: queried through Vercel AI Gateway; Kev-27B v2 scored 52.3 on the same split
benchmarks.harness: the Kev project's own frozen suite; the Kev author builds a competing open model

sources.quote: 64k tokens per request; 32k tokens for `state` plus the longest question
Charged per input token. Output tokens are free.
Our first public model is Jev, available today in early access.
Jev currently accepts text input only.
For example, connect through an AI gateway using its API key and model ID.
Jev 1.13.0 leads the Jev-class systems with 80.0.
Jev’s three setups moved by 2 to 3 points between identical runs

unknown: context_window: TypeSafe gives '64k tokens per request' (state plus every question) and 32k for state plus the longest question, with no exact token count; OpenRouter and Cloudflare list 32K
max_output: does not apply; Jev returns typed answers (a choice, a probability or a score), not generated tokens
SWE-Bench Pro (Scale, public V2): does not apply; Jev cannot write code or text
Terminal-Bench 4.0: does not apply; Jev cannot run an agent loop that produces commands
Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index: does not apply; the index measures generative models
Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index: does not apply; Jev cannot act as a coding agent
METR 50% time horizon: does not apply; Jev cannot carry out a multi-step task
system_card: TypeSafe publishes no system or model card; the nearest documents are the Models page and the jaggedness page
released: 2026-09-15 is the early-access announcement; OpenRouter lists jev-1.13 from 2026-09-18
status: TypeSafe's announcement calls Jev early access, while its Models page calls jev-1.13.0 'the most recent stable, official release'; recorded as preview
